title: Applied ML experiment scratchpad - 2026-03-16
content:
2026-03-16 - quick morning scratchpad (Ethan)

Goal: get a quick apples-to-apples comparison of inference latency, token quality (BLEU/EM/InstrScore), and memory usage across quantization profiles for the Llama-2-13B variant we plan to serve for the small-docs use-case. Verify that 4-bit GPTQ run does not degrade answer correctness on curated prompt-set by >3% and that latency stays < 120ms/token p95 on a single A100-40GB equivalent worker.

Notes / hypotheses:
- q4_k_m (GPTQ) should keep most of the quality with big wins in memory. But some prompts with arithmetic / precise outputs degrade.
- q8_0 (bitsandbytes) is fast and stable, but memory not as low as GPTQ-4bit.
- pref quantize KV cache separately? try separate quantization for weights vs KV if tooling allows.

Model variants tested (run IDs):
- base: llama-2-13b-chat (fp16) -> run R2026-03-16-fp16
- bnb-8: llama-2-13b-chat q8_0 (bitsandbytes) -> run R2026-03-16-q8
- gptq-4: llama-2-13b-chat GPTQ q4_k_m -> run R2026-03-16-q4_gptq
- q4f16: q4_f16 variant (if convertable) -> run R2026-03-16-q4f16

Prompt sets (small curated):
1) factual-recall (50 examples) - short Q/A where exact phrase match matters
2) numeric-arith (30 examples) - arithmetic and table-like outputs
3) instruction-following (40 examples) - multi-step tasks requiring step ordering
4) long-context summarization (10 examples) - 1k-token context, 100-token summary target

Evaluation metrics to collect per run:
- EM (exact match) for factual-recall
- numeric-exact for numeric-arith (tolerance where appropriate)
- instr-score (human-proxy: instruction-following score from eval harness)
- BLEU/ROUGE for summarization + qualitative check
- latency p50/p90/p95 end-to-end (client->response final token)
- tokens/sec and GPU memory peak (nvidia-smi snapshot)
- CPU usage (dataplane process), batch size effect (1 vs 4), beam size fixed at 1

Commands / notes used: (local dev harness)
- python eval/harness.py --model ./models/llama-2-13b-chat --quant gptq_q4_k_m --prompts data/curated/factual-recall.json --batch 1 --seq 512 --out runs/R2026-03-16-q4_gptq/results.json
- convert GPTQ with: python tools/gptq/convert.py --checkpoint models/llama-2-13b-chat --out models/llama-2-13b-chat-q4gptq --bits 4 --group-size 128
- bitsandbytes load test: from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM; model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained('llama-2-13b-chat', load_in_8bit=True, device_map='auto')

Quick results (first pass, raw):
- fp16 (R2026-03-16-fp16): EM 78.0% | numeric-exact 92% | instr-score 86 | latency p95 210ms/token | GPU mem 36.5GB
- q8 (R2026-03-16-q8): EM 76.5% | numeric-exact 90% | instr-score 84 | latency p95 140ms/token | GPU mem 22.8GB
- q4_gptq (R2026-03-16-q4_gptq): EM 74.1% | numeric-exact 81% | instr-score 80 | latency p95 125ms/token | GPU mem 12.2GB
- q4f16 (R2026-03-16-q4f16 tentative): EM 75.0% | numeric-exact 86% | instr-score 82 | latency p95 130ms/token | GPU mem 14.9GB

Immediate observations:
- GPTQ q4 shows the largest memory wins and meets the latency target for p95 (~125ms) at batch size 1 on our A100-equivalent. However numeric-exact drops notably on arithmetic prompts — need to inspect whether tokenization/float rounding or a model failure on carrying digits.
- q8 has small quality drop vs fp16 but is the simplest to deploy (BNB supported in current runtime).
- FP16 is highest quality but memory cost too high for Dedicated low-cost tier.

Debug TODOs (short):
- [ ] Run per-example diff for numeric-arith for q4_gptq vs fp16 -> produce list of failure examples (E: R2026-03-16-q4_gptq/failures.csv)
- [ ] Try smaller group-size during GPTQ conversion (64 vs 128) for numeric stability on arithmetic prompts (re-convert, re-eval).
- [ ] Test prefix caching behavior: run cold vs warm KV cache for long-context summarization; measure latency difference.
- [ ] Try per-layer hybrid quant: keep first and last 2 layers in fp16, quantize middle layers to q4 (cheap conversion path?)
- [ ] Add step to eval harness to capture top-3 tokens probability mass (for hallucination detection per prompt)
- [ ] Post results CSV to GH run artifacts and invite Maya/Asha for quick triage (link in linked_artifacts)

Notes to remember for deployment constraints:
- Dedicated infra wants stable libs -> prefer bitsandbytes q8 path if we cannot certify GPTQ toolchain. But quantized model size for q8 still ~20-24GB vs GPTQ ~10-13GB -> cost delta matters.
- If we can get numeric-exact back within 2% by group-size tuning, GPTQ looks best for cost. Otherwise fallback q8 is safer.

Qual checks / random examples (copy from run):
- prompt: "Calculate 17 * 24"
  - fp16 -> "408" (correct)
  - q4_gptq -> "400" (off) -> check tokenization of numbers (maybe used scientific notation or separator)
- prompt instruct: "Summarize the following paragraph in 2 bullets" -> q4_gptq tends to drop a minor detail once per 20 examples (acceptable?)

Longer-term experiments to schedule:
- run chain-of-thought prompting vs single-shot for numeric-arith under q4 to see if prompting mitigates wrong arithmetic (cheap to test, could be a workaround without re-quantizing).
- test q4 quantization with pfv (post-finetune with LoRA) to see if small fine-tune closes gap (need compute budget).

Commands for baseline artifact upload (to GH actions artifacts):
- tar -czf results-R2026-03-16-q4_gptq.tgz runs/R2026-03-16-q4_gptq/* ; gh release upload --repo redwood-inference/model-ops v0.23 runs.tar.gz

Slack notes (to ping): @Maya Patel - can you eyeball the numeric-exact sample diffs once I attach failures.csv? @Asha Rao - any preference on recommended bitsandbytes version for prod? I used 0.40.0 for today's runs.

Housekeeping / next steps (for my TODO list):
- Today: run group-size=64 GPTQ convert + full eval on numeric-arith (target finish EOD 3/16).
- Tomorrow: run caching experiment + batch size sweep (1/2/4) on q4 and q8, collect latency curves.
- Draft short one-pager for product (Dedicated capacity options) comparing cost/latency/quality across quant profiles (include numbers above).

Unresolved questions:
- Does Redwood's runtime support serving GPTQ models with continuous KV caching now? If not, need eng-rt tracker.
- Is there an easy way to snapshot calibration stats during GPTQ conversion to explain numeric errors?

References / links used: see linked_artifacts. Also: notes in CONFLUENCE:inference/quantization-notes for background conversion scripts.

End of scratchpad.

-- Ethan
